brief: Goldman's Prime Services weekly (Sept 11-17) reports the GS Equity Fundamental L/S Performance Estimate fell 1.02% versus MSCI World TR up 0.35%, driven by -0.95% alpha from long-side losses and -0.07% beta. The GS Equity Systematic L/S estimate rose 1.28%, driven by +1.21% alpha from short-side gains and +0.07% beta. Overall book gross leverage rose 4.6pts to 309.2% (65th percentile, 1-year) and net leverage rose 0.7pts to 77.5% (34th percentile); the L/S ratio fell to 1.670 (25th percentile). Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose to 207.7%, net to 56.4%. Global equities were net bought (+0.5 SDs), long buys outpacing short sales 3.9-to-1, led by North America and Europe against Asia selling; Macro Products were bought while Single Stocks were modestly sold. Communication Services, Consumer Discretionary and Industrials were most bought; Health Care, Energy and Info Tech most sold. Two standalone stories: European equities were net bought at the fastest pace in 5 months (short covers driving, led by Germany/France/Ireland), while global Energy was net sold at the fastest pace in 4 months (roughly equal short and long sales).
